title: Equivalence of module-valued sheaves with constant-ring module sheaves
statement: Let X be a scheme with its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and let r be any natural number, including zero. The category of sheaves valued in modules over the single lift of ZMod r [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] is equivalent to the category of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over the constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] of the double lift of ZMod r. There exists such an equivalence E together with a natural isomorphism from the underlying-abelian-sheaf functor on the first category to E followed by the underlying-abelian-sheaf functor on the second. No injectivity condition is imposed.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Lemma 18.11.1: simultaneous sheafification of a ring presheaf and its modules; specialize the ring presheaf to the constant presheaf. The equivalence is the explicit constant-ring specialization of this construction.

proof.text: Identify the single and double lifts of ZMod r using ULift.ringEquiv. Compose the induced isomorphism of constant ring presheaves with the sheafification unit, giving scalarUnit. This ring map is locally injective and locally surjective: the first factor is an isomorphism, the second is a sheafification unit.

Convert presheaves of modules over the constant coefficient ring to module-valued presheaves: the semilinear restriction maps are linear because the scalar restriction maps are identities. The conversion is full, as natural transformations have exactly the same componentwise linearity and naturality requirements. Compose scalar restriction with this conversion and lift to sheaves, since forgetting to abelian groups preserves and detects the sheaf condition. This defines restriction, which commutes identically with the underlying abelian-sheaf functor. Faithfulness follows from the latter functor. Fullness follows from Mathlib PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction and its invertible counit, which make SheafOfModules.forget followed by scalar restriction full, together with fullness of the constant-presheaf conversion and faithfulness of the inclusion of module-valued sheaves into presheaves.

For a module-valued sheaf N, form its presheaf of modules P over the constant coefficient ring and take M = PresheafOfModules.sheafification scalarUnit P. The module-sheafification adjunction unit gives P -> restriction(M). Its underlying abelian map is the ordinary sheafification unit of P. Since the abelian presheaf of N is already a sheaf, this map is an isomorphism. Forgetting module scalars reflects isomorphisms, so N is isomorphic to restriction(M). Thus restriction is essentially surjective and, being full and faithful, is an equivalence. Take its inverse equivalence for E. Whisker the counit isomorphism with the underlying abelian-sheaf functor and compose with the restriction forgetful comparison to obtain the required natural isomorphism. Every construction is valid for r = 0, r = 1 and the empty scheme.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 18.11.1, implemented by Mathlib PresheafOfModules.sheafification and sheafificationAdjunction; constant-ring encoding and equivalence packaging proved in Lean.

lean.statement:
theorem constantRing_moduleSheaf_equivalence (X : Scheme.{u}) (r : ℕ) :
    ∃ E : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology
        (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod r))) ≌
      SheafOfModules.{u + 1}
        ((constantSheaf X.smallEtaleTopology RingCat.{u + 1}).obj
          (RingCat.of (ULift.{u + 1, u} (ULift.{u} (ZMod r))))),
      Nonempty
        (sheafCompose X.smallEtaleTopology
            (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod r)))
              AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) ≅
          E.functor ⋙ SheafOfModules.toSheaf _)
